terms.gloss: deed, act, what someone has done
evidence: Caesar in Cic. Att. 9.16.2: meum factum probārī abs tē
terms.comment: Latin often says what was done with a verb or a relative clause: quod fēcistī, what you did.

terms.gloss: doing, action (as against thought or rest)
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.19: virtūtis enim laus omnis in āctiōne cōnsistit
terms.comment: Action in general rather than a single deed; in law, a lawsuit (see activity).

evidence: Cic. Sen. 17: gubernātōrem in nāvigandō nihil agere
terms.comment: “Take action” is agere or rem agere; nihil agere, to do nothing.

phrases.latin: virtūtis enim laus omnis in āctiōne cōnsistit
phrases.english: for all the praise of virtue lies in action

phrases.latin: atque ego cum ex ipsā rē magnam capiō voluptātem tum meum factum probārī abs tē triumphō gaudiō
phrases.english: and while I take great pleasure in the thing itself, I am overjoyed that you approve of my action

phrases.latin: dīmidium factī, quī coepit, habet; sapere audē, incipe
phrases.english: well begun is half done: dare to be wise, make a start

sources: Lewis & Short: factum · Lewis & Short: actio · Lewis & Short: ago
